text:
maria: quick PSA from nightly bringup — int4 nova-lite produced subtitle timing drift on ja/zh mixed SRTs, cues ~300-700ms early.
yuki: can you paste the reproducer command?
maria: `python tools/eval_subtitles.py --model nova-lite-q4 --quant int4 --input tests/fixtures/multi_ja_zh_srt/ep12.srt --out /tmp/out.srt --log-tokens`
maria: diff example:
Gold:
00:02:10,200 --> 00:02:10,800

Nova-int4:
00:02:09,800 --> 00:02:10,400

maria: token counts differ — gold tokenized into ["00:02:10", ",200", "-->", "00:02:10", ",800"] but int4 decode emitted ["00:02:09,800-->", "00:02:10,400"].
yuki: looks like timecode+arrow got merged into one token by the quantized decoder. float16 ok?
maria: float16 preserve boundaries. int4 logs show token_id 41233 -> "00:02:09,800-->" at step 8.
eval-bot: alert: subtitle_timing_regression delta_mean=-0.48s on branch bringup/nova-lite-q4 for locales [ja, zh-Hans].
sam: assign to @yuki + @maria to bisect; I'll try a host-tokenizer run. can you run with `--force-tokenizer=host-bpe`?
yuki: running now. ETA 12m.
infra-bot: note: if host-bpe avoids merge, consider locking int4 vocab remap until fixed to avoid downstream SRT serializers relying on token offsets.
maria: quick mitigation planned: serializer fallback to regex `\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3}` for timestamps before using token-derived offsets. PR incoming.
sam: thanks — if int4 remains flaky we may pause nova-lite-q4 rollout for captioning customers.
